prioritySections.priorityLabel: Priority 1: Critical Zero-Click Pages at Positions 1-2

tasks.title: Homepage reports as two URLs in Search Console: point the Business Profile link at the canonical URL
tasks.meta: Homepage merged: 34,440 impressions, 138 clicks, position 10.3. Search Console splits it into two rows.
tasks.problem: Search Console reports the homepage as two rows. One row (the http://www address) carries most of the big generic searches ("roofing companies", "roofers") with almost no clicks; the other (the https address) carries the rest. Merged, the homepage is 34,440 impressions and 138 clicks at position 10.3. The site itself is already set up correctly: both addresses 301 to https://valleypeakroof.com/, the canonical tag self-references, and the sitemap and schema use the https address (checked live on September 8).
tasks.rootCause: The http://www row carries the local-pack style searches with almost no clicks, which is the signature of Local Pack and Business Profile impressions, not a duplicate page. Google credits those to whatever URL the Business Profile links to. The likely cause is that the Business Profile website field still uses http://www.valleypeakroof.com/ (to confirm inside the profile). One minor technical item exists: http://www reaches the canonical in two redirect hops instead of one.

changes.before: Website field likely set to http://www.valleypeakroof.com/ (confirm in the profile)
changes.after: Set the Business Profile website field to https://valleypeakroof.com/ so Search Console credits Business Profile impressions and clicks to the canonical URL

changes.before: http://www.valleypeakroof.com/ redirects to https://www, then to https://valleypeakroof.com/ (two hops)
changes.after: Collapse to a single hop in the Netlify domain settings if the platform allows; otherwise leave as is, the chain is harmless

changes.before: Homepage numbers are split across two rows
changes.after: From October, read the homepage as one merged row; the report already merges variants, and the split should disappear once the profile link changes

pendingItems: Open the Business Profile and confirm the website field value before changing it
After the change, watch the http://www row in Search Console fade over the next 4 to 6 weeks
tasks.impact: No ranking change expected. This is a reporting fix: it stops the homepage from looking like a position-19 page and makes month-to-month homepage comparisons clean. It costs one profile edit.

tasks.title: Fix schema validation errors across all 9 audited service and blog pages
tasks.problem: Every single audited page returned a schema validation warning. Invalid structured data means Google cannot generate rich results from these pages, which suppresses CTR for pages that would otherwise qualify for review stars, FAQ dropdowns, or service markup in the SERP.
tasks.rootCause: The automated audit detected validation errors sitewide, suggesting a systemic issue in the schema template rather than page-by-page mistakes. Common causes include missing required properties, incorrect @type values, or malformed JSON-LD that passes visual inspection but fails the Rich Results Test.

changes.before: Schema errors are present but specific broken properties are unconfirmed
changes.after: Run every affected URL through Google Rich Results Test and document the exact error messages before making any changes

changes.after: Implement valid LocalBusiness schema on / with: name, url, telephone, address, areaServed, openingHours, aggregateRating (if review count supports it), and sameAs. Add Service schema on /residential-roof-repairs, /roof-replacement-installation, /commercial-roofing, /siding-installation with: name, provider, areaServed, description

changes.after: Add Article schema to /blog/storm-and-hail-roof-damage-guide, /blog/black-streaks-on-roof-causes, /blog/ice-dam-prevention-roof-leaks-pennsylvania, /blog/berks-county-winter-snow-loads. Add FAQPage schema to any blog page that contains a Q and A section

prioritySections.priorityLabel: Priority 5: Homepage Performance and Low Text Ratio Fix

tasks.title: Homepage — compress images and reduce page size above 1MB flagged in audit
tasks.meta: / — 96/100 audit score | Warning: Large page size over 1MB | Warning: Low text-to-HTML ratio under 10%
tasks.problem: The homepage audit flagged two performance warnings: page size exceeds 1MB and the text-to-HTML ratio is under 10%. A 1MB-plus homepage will load slowly on mobile connections, which is the primary device for local roofing searches. Low text-to-HTML ratio limits how much useful content Google can extract from the page.
tasks.rootCause: Oversized images that have not been compressed to modern formats (WebP), combined with a UI-heavy page design where most of the file size is markup and assets rather than readable content, are the likely causes of both warnings.

changes.before: Homepage images served in original format (likely JPEG/PNG), contributing to 1MB-plus page weight
changes.after: Convert all homepage images to WebP format. Compress to under 100KB per image where quality allows. Add width and height attributes to all img tags to prevent layout shift.

changes.before: CSS and JS files may be unminified and loaded synchronously
changes.after: Minify all CSS and JS files. Move non-critical scripts to load asynchronously or defer. Inline only critical above-the-fold CSS.
